propositions.text: XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Haiti, is appealing against the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Haiti, is appealing against a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting his claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that XXXX XXXX, a Haitian citizen, is appealing the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.

propositions.text: The appellant submits no new evidence and does not request a hearing before the RAD.
propositions.quote: He is not submitting any new evidence in his appeal, nor is he requesting a hearing before the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD).

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the appellant submits no new evidence and requests no hearing before the RAD.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA paragraph 111(1)(a), the RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to paragraph 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD confirms the RPD's determination, namely, that XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" pursuant to section 96 of the IRPA, nor a "person in need of protection" pursuant to section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's decision that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges he left Haiti in 2013 due to threats and assaults by jealous neighbours.
propositions.quote: In his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), the appellant alleges that he left Haiti on XXXX XXXX, 2013, to travel to the Dominican Republic and then to Brazil because he had been threatened and assaulted by his neighbours who were jealous of his success as a XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges he left Haiti in 2013 due to threats and assaults by jealous neighbours.

propositions.text: The appellant claims he was a victim of racism and discrimination at work in Brazil when abandoned by a fellow driver.
propositions.quote: The appellant claims that he was the victim of racism and discrimination at his workplace in Brazil when he was abandoned in a remote city by his fellow driver.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant claims he faced racism and discrimination at work in Brazil when abandoned by a fellow driver.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges witnessing assaults and racism against Haitians in Brazil, leading him to leave for the US in 2016 and then Canada in 2017.
propositions.quote: The appellant alleges that he witnessed assaults and racism directed at Haitians in Brazil, and therefore decided to leave the country and travel to the United States in XXXX 2016, where he remained until July 2017, when he came to Canada and filed a claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges witnessing racism in Brazil, left for the US in 2016, then Canada in 2017 to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant excluded under Article 1E due to permanent resident status in Brazil.
propositions.quote: The RPD determined that the appellant was excluded under Article 1E of the Convention because he had permanent resident status in Brazil.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant had access to state protection in Brazil and failed to prove persecution fear under the Convention.
propositions.quote: The RPD further determined that the appellant had access to state protection in Brazil, that he had failed to establish that his fear of returning to Brazil amounted to persecution within the meaning of the Convention, and that he was therefore not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection."

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant excluded under Article 1E due to permanent resident status and access to protection in Brazil, denying refugee status.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred in applying Article 1E because Haitians in Brazil face hostile, xenophobic conditions unlike nationals.
propositions.quote: The appellant is arguing before the RAD that the RPD erred in concluding that he was excluded under Article 1E of the Convention because, in reality, given the hostile and xenophobic conditions that Haitians face in Brazil, their status is not similar to that of Brazilian nationals.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred applying Article 1E because Haitians in Brazil face hostile conditions unlike nationals.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD failed to give real consideration to the racism he experienced in Brazil.
propositions.quote: The appellant further argues that the RPD erred by not giving [translation] "any real consideration" to the racism he experienced in Brazil.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD failed to properly consider the racism he experienced in Brazil.

propositions.text: The appellant requests the RAD to set aside the RPD's decision and grant refugee protection.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the appellant is asking the RAD to set aside the RPD's determination and grant him refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant asks the RAD to overturn the RPD's decision and grant refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness except for credibility findings, which are reviewed for reasonableness if RPD had a meaningful advantage.
propositions.quote: The role of the RAD is to review RPD decisions on a correctness standard after conducting its own analysis of the record in order to determine whether the RPD erred as the appellant alleges. The exception to this rule arises when the RPD's findings relate to the assessment of the credibility or weight to be given to the oral testimony, in situations where it enjoyed a meaningful advantage. In these situations, the RAD must apply the reasonableness standard of review (Canada v. Huruglica, F.C.A. No. A-470-14). If I find that the RPD enjoyed a meaningful advantage, I will explain how in my analysis.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reviews RPD decisions on correctness, except credibility findings reviewed for reasonableness if RPD had meaningful advantage.

propositions.text: The first issue is whether the RPD erred in concluding the appellant's permanent resident status in Brazil grants rights similar to nationals, triggering Article 1E.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the first matter to be determined in the present case is whether the RPD erred in concluding that the appellant's permanent resident status in Brazil grants him rights similar to those of Brazilian nationals and that Article 1E of the Convention therefore applies to him.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the issue whether the RPD erred in concluding the appellant's permanent resident status grants rights similar to nationals under Article 1E.

propositions.text: The court finds the RPD did not err in its conclusion on the appellant's status and Article 1E.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the RPD did not err, for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD did not err regarding the appellant's status and Article 1E.

propositions.text: The appellant's argument about discrimination despite permanent resident status was not raised before the RPD or questioned by counsel.
propositions.quote: The appellant stated that the discrimination and racism that Haitians face in Brazil is such that even permanent resident status does not grant them rights similar to those of Brazilian nationals. I note that this argument was not invoked by the appellant or his counsel before the RPD, and his counsel did not question him on this subject before the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant did not raise or have counsel question him on discrimination despite permanent resident status before the RPD.

propositions.text: The appellant claims Haitians with permanent resident status in Brazil face discrimination affecting access to employment, housing, education, travel, social benefits, and freedom of expression.
propositions.quote: In paragraph 13 of the appellant's memorandum, he claims that Haitians who have permanent resident status in Brazil do not benefit from rights similar to those of Brazilian nationals because [translation] "they endure discrimination based on their race and nationality, which affects their ability to benefit from equal access to employment, housing, property rights, education, travel (and) social benefits such as access to medical care and freedom of expression."

paragraphs.summary: The appellant claims Haitians with permanent resident status in Brazil face discrimination limiting access to many rights and benefits.

propositions.text: No evidence shows the appellant made the allegation of discrimination affecting rights as claimed in his memorandum.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, nothing in the evidence shows that the appellant made such an allegation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no evidence the appellant made the alleged discrimination claims in the record.

propositions.text: The appellant testified he was employed in Brazil and employers prefer Haitians as better employees than Brazilians.
propositions.quote: On the contrary, the appellant testified that he was employed in Brazil and that employers generally prefer to hire Haitians because they are allegedly better employees than Brazilians.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant testified he was employed and employers prefer Haitians over Brazilians.

propositions.text: The appellant never alleged denial of housing, education, travel, social benefits, medical care, or freedom of expression.
propositions.quote: At no point did the appellant allege that he was denied the right to housing, education, travel or social benefits such as medical care or freedom of expression.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant never alleged denial of housing, education, travel, social benefits, medical care, or freedom of expression.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows permanent residents in Brazil have rights to work, study, and access social services.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence submitted in this file (see Tab 3.4 of the National Documentation Package (NDP) for Brazil dated March 31, 2017), as noted in the RPD's reasons, indicates that permanent residents in Brazil have the right to work, study and have access to social services.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes documentary evidence that permanent residents in Brazil have rights to work, study, and social services.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err concluding the appellant's status is similar to Brazilian nationals and Article 1E applies.
propositions.quote: I am therefore of the opinion that the RPD did not err in concluding that the appellant's status in Brazil is essentially similar to that of a Brazilian national and that he is therefore a person referred to in Article 1E of the Convention.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD did not err in finding the appellant's status similar to nationals and applying Article 1E.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by giving no real consideration to racism endured in Brazil and should have examined claimant's particular circumstances.
propositions.quote: the appellant also argues that the RPD erred by giving "no real consideration" to the racism that he endured in Brazil, and he adds that, [translation] "the panel should have examined the claimant's particular circumstances."

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by not properly considering racism he endured in Brazil and his particular circumstances.

propositions.text: Unclear whether appellant's argument concerns fear of returning to Brazil or exclusion under Article 1E of the Convention.
propositions.quote: It is also unclear to me whether this argument pertains to the appellant's fear of returning to Brazil or is a continuation of his previous observation that he should not be excluded under Article 1E of the Convention.

propositions.text: The court is unsure it understands the appellant's argument.
propositions.quote: I am not sure that I understand this argument.

paragraphs.summary: The court is unsure it understands the appellant's argument or whether it concerns fear of return or exclusion under Article 1E.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err in concluding appellant's fear of returning to Brazil is not a fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that the RPD did not err in concluding that the appellant's fear of returning to Brazil is not equivalent to a fear of persecution, for the following reasons.

propositions.text: Second issue to be decided is whether RPD erred on appellant's fear of returning to Brazil.
propositions.quote: this is the second issue to be decided in this case

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the second issue is whether the RPD erred on fear of return and concludes the RPD did not err.

propositions.text: Appellant describes one racist and discriminatory incident where co-worker abandoned him in a remote city.
propositions.quote: there is only one incident that he describes as racist and discriminatory. The appellant alleged that his co-worker abandoned him in a remote city and that he had to find his own way home.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant described one racist incident where a co-worker abandoned him in a remote city.

propositions.text: Appellant explained co-worker hoped appellant would be fired to give job to co-worker's friend; employer blamed co-worker.
propositions.quote: the appellant explained that he later found out that his co-worker had hoped that the appellant would be fired so that his job could be given back to one of his co-worker's friends. In the end, the employer blamed the co-worker and threatened to fire him if it happened again.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant explained co-worker wanted his job for a friend; employer blamed co-worker and threatened firing.

propositions.text: The incident is isolated and not caused by appellant's race or nationality but by co-worker's desire to give job to friend.
propositions.quote: not only is this is an isolated incident, but the evidence also shows that the appellant's race or nationality were not the cause of it; the appellant's co-worker wanted his friend to have the appellant's job.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the incident isolated and not racially motivated but due to co-worker's personal motives.

propositions.text: Appellant stated two Haitians in his neighbourhood were shot and killed.
propositions.quote: the appellant also stated that two Haitians in his neighbourhood had been shot and killed.

propositions.text: Nothing suggests these killings were related to racism or discrimination as alleged by appellant.
propositions.quote: nothing in the evidence suggests that these incidents were related to racism or discrimination, as the appellant alleged.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant stated two Haitians were killed, but court finds no evidence these were racially motivated.

propositions.text: RAD considered documentary evidence on discrimination against Afro-Brazilians in Brazil from RPD record.
propositions.quote: The RAD has taken into account the documentary evidence in the RPD's record regarding discrimination against Afro-Brazilians in Brazil

propositions.text: Appellant did not submit or cite other documentation on discrimination before RPD or RAD.
propositions.quote: the appellant did not submit or cite any other documentation on this subject, either before the RPD or the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD considered documentary evidence on Afro-Brazilian discrimination; appellant submitted no other documentation.

propositions.text: Appellant has not established a well-founded fear of persecution due to race or serious violation of fundamental rights.
propositions.quote: the appellant has not established that the incidents he experienced and the overall situation for members of his ethnic group give rise to a well-founded fear of persecution by reason of his race

propositions.text: Appellant has not shown discrimination in Brazil would make his life unbearable.
propositions.quote: the appellant has not demonstrated that the discrimination he could potentially face in Brazil would make his life in that country unbearable.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellant has not shown a well-founded fear of persecution or unbearable discrimination in Brazil.

propositions.text: Appellant has not established on balance of probabilities a risk to his life under section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: appellant has not established on a balance of probabilities that he would be subjected to a risk to his life, in accordance with section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant has not shown a risk to his life under section 97 of IRPA.

propositions.text: Appellant does not dispute RPD's conclusion that he has access to state protection in Brazil.
propositions.quote: the appellant does not dispute the RPD's conclusion that he has access to state protection in Brazil.

propositions.text: RPD's brief analysis on state protection need not be further assessed given court's conclusions.
propositions.quote: The RPD's analysis on this point is brief, and in light of my conclusions above, it is not necessary for me to further assess whether the RPD erred in its analysis.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant does not dispute state protection access; court finds no need to reassess RPD's analysis on this.

propositions.text: Appellant has not shown RPD made errors warranting RAD intervention.
propositions.quote: I conclude that the appellant has not demonstrated that the RPD made errors that warrant the RAD's intervention.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellant has not shown RPD errors warranting RAD intervention.

propositions.text: RPD's determination that appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection is confirmed.
propositions.quote: I confirm the RPD's determination, namely, that XXXX XXXX is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's determination that appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
